market_holds: Spot $4.04 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-13). The stock is down 19.5% over 5 sessions, 12.6% over 20 and 26% since the $5.48 close of 2026-10-13 (implied by the FSI warrant strike $5.754 = 105% of that close, 8-K filed 2026-10-20). It sits 2.8% above its 52-week low and 90% below its high. There is no usable option chain (no paired strikes), so the usual move is the median of 7 past reactions, 5.98%; 5 of those 7 were down. 20-day realised vol is 81% annualised, and the stock trades about 63k shares, roughly $250k, a day. Consensus is effectively absent: Benzinga shows a Q3 revenue figure of $2.8m against the company's own $8-11m guide, and no analyst asked a question on the Q2 call. So the line the stock trades on is the company's guide: Q3 revenue $8-11m and adjusted EBITDA $(9)-(13)m; FY26 revenue $50-55m and adjusted EBITDA $(22)-(26)m (Q2 release, 2026-08-14). Valuation is dominated by its 33.52m H shares of Shougang LanzaTech (HK:2553). At HK$12.27 (2026-11-12) those are worth about $53m. That is about the basic market cap of $53m on 13.09m shares and below the fully diluted $84m that includes Khosla's 7.8m penny warrants. Khosla controls 58.4% (13D/A, 2026-11-06). Short interest is 3.5% of shares, 6 days to cover (sweep row, FINRA 2026-10-30).
view: This print has two parts, and only one of them is unknown. The known part is the mark on SGLT. Its stock fell from HK$52.20 on 2026-06-30 to HK$13.26 on 2026-09-30, so Q3 will carry an unrealised loss of about $168m on the stake. The headline will be a net loss of roughly $175-180m, around -$13 a share, against a Q2 net income of $184m. That is pure arithmetic on a public HK quote and in principle is priced. Still, nano-cap headline readers and data feeds will show it as an enormous 'miss'. The Q2 precedent says that does not drive the reaction: Q2 also showed an aggregator 'miss' on EPS and revenue, and the stock rose 2.09%. The unknown part is the FY26 guide. H1 revenue was $21.0m and the Q3 guide is $8-11m, so the FY range needs Q4 revenue of $18-26m, against a quarterly run-rate of about $9-12m. It also needs Q4 adjusted EBITDA of about breakeven, against -$7.6m in Q2. The only named driver is certified-ethanol sales 'beginning in Q4' (CFO on the Q2 call). The ISCC EU certification that unlocks them did arrive on 2026-10-21, but no sale, customer or volume has been announced. A cut or a soft reaffirmation is more likely than a clean hold, and this company withdrew guidance once before. Against that, the stock has already fallen 19.5% in five sessions on no company news while SGLT was roughly flat (HK$12.80 on 11-06 to HK$12.27 on 11-12). It trades at an EV close to the value of the SGLT stake alone, so the operating business, cash of roughly $35-40m (my estimate from $48.9m at 6/30 less a guided $9-13m EBITDA loss) and the LanzaJet stake are valued near nothing. A cut lands on a price that has partly de-risked. A hold, or news of SGLT monetisation (the six-month mark from the 2026-06-03 listing falls around 12-03), could pop a stock this thin. Overall I lean slightly down: the guide arithmetic is stretched and past reactions skew negative. But the pre-print selloff and the stake-backed floor keep the lean small, and the size is set more by illiquidity and Monday's HK tape for SGLT than by anything I can sign.
unpriced: Possibly the FY26 guide's dependence on a Q4 of $18-26m revenue at breakeven EBITDA. Nobody covering the stock has done that arithmetic in public: no analyst questions on the Q2 call, and the aggregator consensus is nonsensical. But the 19.5% fall into the print on no news may already reflect it, so I cannot show it is unpriced.

recommendation.reason: The best-supported mechanism is a likely FY26 guide cut, since the range needs a Q4 roughly double the run-rate at breakeven EBITDA. The stock is uncovered, so a cut would be news. But the stock has already dropped 19.5% in five sessions into the print on no company news, and it trades at about the value of its listed SGLT stake. A cut may be partly in the price, and a hold would surprise upward. That leaves my probability well short of 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A reaffirmed FY26 revenue range backed by a named certified-ethanol sale or contract, or an announced plan to monetise part of the SGLT stake for cash. Either would push p_up well above 50.

self_critique: The guide-cut thesis is my arithmetic. Management knew H1 was $21m when it set $50-55m in August, so it may have a lumpy Q4 item (an engineering milestone, a licence or a certified-ethanol contract) that it can see and I cannot, and reaffirming it would be a positive surprise on a depressed stock. Equally, the -$168m SGLT mark could make the headline look catastrophic to the feeds that drive thin nano-caps, which argues for a stronger down lean than 43. In both directions the window's move may be dominated by Monday's SGLT trading in Hong Kong and by order-flow noise in a $250k-a-day stock.
